title: Telemetry-driven SSE reconnect heuristics and orphan-chunk garbage collection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement an SSE reconnection strategy that leverages runtime telemetry to pick optimal backoff, hedging, and resume semantics, while introducing a robust orphan-chunk garbage-collection policy to prevent unbounded memory growth and avoid serving stale/misordered fragments for function calls and structured JSON outputs.
acceptance_criteria:
[1] Server exposes new telemetry metrics (sse.reconnect_attempts, sse.orphan_chunk_count, sse.resume_success_rate).
[2] Client/server negotiation allows a max-retention header (X-Resume-Retention-ms) and server enforces configured retention.
[3] Orphan chunks older than retention are garbage-collected and emit audit log entries.
[4] No regression in structured functioncall end-to-end tests (tool-calling order preserved) under reconnection stress.
[5] Load test shows <5% increase in median memory per connection compared to baseline for 99th percentile connection durations.
implementation_notes: Design favors incremental rollout: start with conservative default retention (10s), enable telemetry-driven tuning in a canary group. Heuristics: if resume_success_rate > 95% on a route, reduce retention to improve resource reuse; if orphan_chunk_count persistently > threshold, increase retention for that route and trigger a diagnostic trace. Use a per-connection circular buffer indexed by sequence number and token-offset; add tombstone markers for chunks that are logically consumed. Avoid global GC sweeps; GC runs per-shard to maintain throughput. Ensure compatibility with JSONL/length-prefixed frames and toolcall frame boundaries by never collecting chunks until all dependent toolcall markers are acknowledged or timeout expires.
tradeoffs: Conservative retention reduces memory pressure but risks making resumption less reliable for bursty mobile clients. Aggressive retention increases memory/latency but improves resume success. We prefer a telemetry-first approach so we can adapt per-route. Adding per-connection metadata increases metadata overhead and slightly more CPU, but avoids expensive global reconciliation logic.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for buffer pinning and tombstones. 2) Integration test that simulates: client sends fragments, disconnects mid-toolcall, reconnects with resume token; verify ordering and no duplicate tool invocations. 3) Chaos test: fleet of clients reconnecting with randomized jitter to validate backoff heuristics. 4) Memory soak: 24h stress with long-lived connections to validate GC reduces orphan_chunk_count to stable baseline.
